• Scientific name: Rhadinoloricaria bahuaja (Chang & Castro, 1999)
  • Synonym: Crossoloricaria bahuaja
  • IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated
South America: Madre de Dios basin in Peru, Rio Grande in Bolivia and Rio Manuripe in Pando. Type locality: Río Tambopata, Tambopata Province, Departamento Madre de Dios, Peru.
Occurs in the main river and major tributaries, always over sandy beaches.
Stomach contents of fish examined in the wild include larvae of aquatic insects, small seeds and debris.

Distinguished from all other species of Crossoloricaria by having more teeth (4–8 premaxillary and 8–11 mandibular teeth), more coalescing plates (17–20), a longer maxillary barbel (68–109% HL) reaching the middle or proximal third of the pectoral fin, more developed barbels of the lower lip (16–27% HL), and a greater interorbital width (16–21% HL). The first ray of the dorsal, pectoral and pelvic fins is produced beyond the branched fin rays.
